sentences.text: Albertaceratops was a centrosaurine horned dinosaur living in Alberta, Canada, during the Upper Cretaceous period.
This animal is unusual because it combined long brow horns with the typical skull structure found in other members of its group.
It also featured a bony ridge over its nose and two large hooks projecting outward from the back of its head.
Scientists estimate this creature grew to a length of 5.8 meters and weighed 3500 kilograms.
Knowledge of the animal comes mainly from a nearly complete skull, leaving the rest of its skeleton poorly understood.
The type specimen was a single complete skull discovered in August 2001, along with some scattered bone fragments.
The species name honors Cecil Nesmo, a local rancher who helped fossil hunters find the remains.
Phylogenetic analysis by Michael J. Ryan classifies Albertaceratops as the most basal member of the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
Albertaceratops lived approximately 77.5 million years ago.
This places it within the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, a time spanning roughly 84 to 71 million years ago.
It is debated whether specimens from the Judith River Formation in Montana belong to Albertaceratops, as further study attributed them to the different centrosaurine Medusaceratops.
